info.title: GroundTruth
info.description: Independent causal verification for climate restoration and carbon-credit claims. This API returns evidence bundles with full provenance, not bare scores. A divergence between an independent estimate and a developer claim is a trigger for accredited review, never a finding of fraud.

get.summary: List stored runs, newest first
get.description:
Runs matching the filters, newest first, in pages.

Pagination is by cursor, not offset: the sort key (`created_at`, `run_id`) never
changes, so runs written while you page cannot shift or repeat a page. A run whose
write commits late can be missing from the scroll in progress and appears in the
next one. There is no total count; it would be stale as soon as it was read.

Only runs filed under a project the active organization owns or has been granted are
listed; the scope is applied here, never taken from the query.

get.summary: Compare two runs by evidence id
get.description:
A per-evidence-id diff: each id is `added`, `removed`, `changed` or `unchanged`.

**NOT COMPARABLE.** When the runs are for different cases, differ in data mode or
engine version, were written under incompatible contracts, or one has no evidence
bundle (refused, failed, queued, cancelled), the response says `comparable: false`
with every reason and returns **no diff**. A difference across engine versions is
not presented as a change. Runs from different specifications are comparable, with
`same_specification: false`.

Both runs must be filed under projects the caller can read with diagnostics access (the
comparison exposes evidence values); otherwise the pair is `404`, or `403` when the
project is visible but the level is too low.

get.summary: Fetch one stored run
get.description:
One run with its outcome and, when it has one, its evidence bundle.

A refused run returns `200` with `result_state: "refused"` and the structured
error (code, stage, message, remediation, detail). A run still queued or running
returns its state with no bundle.

With `include_report=true` a run that has a bundle also carries `report_markdown`,
rendered on read by the deterministic renderer. No language model narrates a
stored run.

The run is authorized through its project. The evidence bundle and the report built from
it carry the causal diagnostics, so they are returned only to an owner or `audit` grant;
other levels get the same run without those two fields (redaction removes fields and
never changes values). `404` when the run is missing, unfiled, or in a project the caller
cannot see.

post.description:
Queue a simulated analysis for a case and return at once; poll `status_url`.

* **`202`**: a new job was queued.
* **`200`**: nothing new was queued. Either a stored result already answers this exact
  request (`from_cache`), or an identical job is already in flight (`deduplicated`).
  `run_id` is that existing run.

Only simulated data can run, and the response says so (`is_simulated`, `notice`).
`synthetic: false` is refused with `501`; it is never quietly simulated. There is no
`true_effect` field: it is not part of the specification hash, so accepting it would
let two different simulations share one cached answer.

The case must belong to a project the caller's organization owns, and the caller's role
must allow starting runs; the run is recorded with the caller as `requested_by`.

200.description: An existing result or job answers it.

404.description: Unknown case, or no access to its project.

422.description: The body is invalid (a validation error), or `min_donors` is below the case's floor (`min_donors_below_case_floor`).

429.description: Over the per-user analysis submission limit (`too_many_submissions`, shared with `/verify`). See `Retry-After`.

get.summary: A job's status and progress
get.description:
Where a job is, cheap enough to poll about once a second until `terminal` is true.

`stages` are what was observed as the job moved through the worker: claim, data access,
the engine, recording. The engine is one uninterruptible step, so its internal timings
(`engine_metrics`) appear only after it finishes, and there is **no percentage** at any
point. While the engine runs you get its `elapsed_ms`, which is time spent, not
progress. A **refusal** is `succeeded` with `result_state: "refused"`: the job worked.

post.description:
Stop a job.

* **queued** → `200`, `cancelled` at once; no worker will start it.
* **running** → `202`, still `running` with `cancel_requested: true`. The engine is one
  uninterruptible step, so the worker honours the request when it reaches a checkpoint
  or the engine returns; the result is then discarded and the job ends `cancelled`.
* **already cancelled**, or cancel already requested → the same answer again.
* **succeeded or failed** → `409 job_already_finished`; nothing changes.

get.summary: Stream a job's progress (SSE)
get.description:
Emit a `progress` event with the full job view on every change, then a final `done`.

The stream ends once the job is terminal. Unknown jobs are `404` and an unavailable
store is `503` before any event is sent, exactly as for `GET /jobs/{run_id}`. So is a job
in a project the caller cannot read: authorization comes first, then the stream.

post.description: Checks the credentials and sets the `gt_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax; Secure behind HTTPS). Send that cookie on every later request. A wrong email or password are indistinguishable (`invalid_credentials`, 401); 5 failures for one email from one address in 15 minutes are refused with `too_many_attempts` (429, `Retry-After`).

post.description:
Create, calibrate and register a new project case.

Everything is validated before anything is written. A rejected case answers a structured
422 (`invalid_case`, with the field named, or `case_status_requires_review`) and leaves
no file behind. Cases are always created as `scaffolded`. Sign-in is always required, and
the creation is audited (`case.create`).

422.description: The body is invalid (a validation error), or the case is refused with a structured code and the offending field: `invalid_case` or `case_status_requires_review`.

get.summary: One case in full
get.description: Return one case definition in full.

post.summary: Run a verification now and wait for the result
post.description:
Run the verification pipeline for a case.

Needs what starting a job needs: a role that may start runs in the organization that owns
the case's project. The run is audited (`run.start`).

Synchronous today. The analysis job lifecycle (queue, poll, cancel) is
tracked separately; this endpoint keeps the same response shape so the
frontend contract does not change when it moves behind a job.

422.description: Either the request body is invalid (a validation error), or the engine refused or rejected the request (an engine failure, where `is_refusal` says which). A refusal is a legitimate outcome, not a malfunction.

429.description: Over the per-user analysis submission limit (`too_many_submissions`, shared with `POST /jobs`). See `Retry-After`.

501.description: Not implemented: observed data (a plain message), or a capability the engine does not have (an engine failure).

503.description: A required dataset could not be retrieved.

get.summary: Download a case's evidence bundle as CSV
get.description:
Export the case's evidence bundle as a UTF-8 CSV attachment.

Every evidence item with its value, unit, uncertainty and provenance fingerprint. The
`X-GroundTruth-Data-Mode` header and the `# is_simulated` line say whether the data is
simulated. Audited (`export.download`).

200.description: A UTF-8 CSV: provenance header lines starting with `#`, then one row per evidence item.

X-GroundTruth-Data-Mode.description: `simulated` or `observed`: what the exported data is.

403.description: Your role may not export (`forbidden`).

404.description: Unknown case, or no access to its project.

get.summary: Download a case's verified screening report as PDF
get.description:
Export the case's screening verification report as a self-contained PDF attachment.

The report is verified against its own evidence bundle before it is exported, and the PDF
says which generator wrote it. Without ``narrate`` it is the deterministic report.

parameters.name: narrate

schema.description: Narrate the report with the configured GenAI provider. The narration is verified against the bundle first, and the export is refused (never substituted) if it fails.

parameters.description: Narrate the report with the configured GenAI provider. The narration is verified against the bundle first, and the export is refused (never substituted) if it fails.

ConclusionView.description: One layered conclusion, or why it cannot be drawn.

level.title: Level

Confidence.title: Confidence
Confidence.description:
An interval estimate with an explicit interpretation.

``kind`` records whether the interval is a classical confidence interval, a
permutation-based range, or a sensitivity envelope. Reporting these as if
they were interchangeable would be misleading.

name.title: Name
name.description: Project name, 2 to 120 characters. The case id is derived from it unless `case_id` is given.

country.title: Country
country.description: Country the project lies in, 2 to 80 characters.

registry_id.title: Registry Id
registry_id.description: The project's registry identifier, 2 to 60 characters.

area_ha.title: Area Ha
area_ha.description: Declared project area in hectares; must be positive.

crediting_period_start.title: Crediting Period Start
crediting_period_start.description: First day of the crediting period, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

crediting_period_end.title: Crediting Period End
crediting_period_end.description: Last day of the crediting period, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

claimed_credits_tco2e.title: Claimed Credits Tco2E
claimed_credits_tco2e.description:
Credits the developer claims, in tCO2e, if known. Shown beside the evidence, never used to
compute it.

donor_pool_size.title: Donor Pool Size
donor_pool_size.description: Candidate donor areas to draw, 10 to 100.

pre_end.title: Pre End
pre_end.description: Last pre-treatment year; must come before `post_start`.

boundary_geojson.title: Boundary Geojson
boundary_geojson.description: Project boundary as GeoJSON. Optional; validated before anything is written.

case_id.title: Case Id
case_id.description: Choose the case id instead of deriving it from `name`. Must be unique.

status.title: Status
status.description: Not settable. Cases created here are always 'scaffolded'; omit this field. Sending 'analysed' is refused with `case_status_requires_review`, because that status needs a run reviewed by both owners (C7, #4), and any other value is refused with `invalid_case`.

CreateCaseRequest.description: Request to define and register a new project case.

CreateOrgRequest.title: CreateOrgRequest
CreateOrgRequest.description: A new organization; you become its owner.

DataSourceMode.title: DataSourceMode
DataSourceMode.description: Execution mode: synthetic benchmark vs genuine real observations.

version.title: Version
version.description: Provider version or snapshot date, e.g. '2024.1'.

source_uri.title: Source Uri
source_uri.description: Where the dataset was read from, when recorded.

retrieved_at.title: Retrieved At
retrieved_at.description: ISO timestamp of retrieval, set by the platform.

DatasetRef.title: DatasetRef
DatasetRef.description:
A pinned reference to an external dataset.

The platform resolves a logical dataset name to a concrete, versioned
reference before the engine runs. The engine never chooses a dataset
version, so a re-run months later uses the same imagery rather than
whatever the provider currently serves.

changed.title: Changed
changed.description: Ids in both whose content differs.

unchanged.title: Unchanged
unchanged.description: Ids in both with identical content.

DiffSummary.title: DiffSummary
DiffSummary.description: How many ids fall in each status.

trajectory.title: Trajectory
trajectory.description: Status of the vegetation trajectory dimension.

risk.title: Risk
risk.description: Status of the ecological risk dimension.

DimensionStatuses.title: DimensionStatuses
DimensionStatuses.description: The status of each assessment dimension, for a portfolio row.

status.title: Status
status.description:
A change status (Improving, Deteriorating, Stable, Mixed spatial performance, Elevated
ecological risk, No clear change, Insufficient evidence) for dimensions 1-6; a High/Moderate/Low
rating for dimension 7; an attribution verdict (Supported, Not supported, Inconclusive) for
dimension 8.

status_kind.title: Status Kind
status_kind.description: What `status` means: a change status (dimensions 1-6), an evidence-quality rating (7) or an attribution verdict (8).

suggested.title: Suggested
suggested.description: What the evidence suggests but does not establish.

limitation.title: Limitation
limitation.description:
The main limitation: missing_data, weak_statistical_power, poor_reference_comparability,
climate_confounding, failed_model_assumptions or none.

evidence_needed.title: Evidence Needed
evidence_needed.description: What evidence would strengthen the finding.

evidence_refs.title: Evidence Refs
evidence_refs.description: References to observations, climate records and other dimensions.

DimensionView.title: DimensionView
DimensionView.description: One of the eight assessment dimensions.

is_refusal.title: Is Refusal
is_refusal.description: The same value as `detail.is_refusal`, at the top level.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Identifier of this request, also in the `X-Request-ID` header.

EngineFailureBody.title: EngineFailureBody
EngineFailureBody.description: The body ``/verify`` returns when the engine refused or could not run.

code.description:
The engine's error code. `insufficient_data` and `donor_pool_inadequate` are refusals; the
rest are errors.

message.title: Message
message.description: Plain-language explanation, safe to show a user.

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: The engine stage that refused or failed.

is_refusal.title: Is Refusal
is_refusal.description:
True when the engine declined to estimate because the data cannot support a reliable number.
A legitimate outcome, not a malfunction.

remediation.title: Remediation
remediation.description: What could be done about it, when the engine knows.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: Identifier of the engine run that refused or failed.

EngineFailureDetail.title: EngineFailureDetail
EngineFailureDetail.description:
Why ``/verify`` returned no result: the engine refused, or could not run.

``is_refusal`` is the field that matters. A refusal is the system correctly declining
to produce a fragile number, and is shown as a legitimate outcome, not as an error.

available.title: Available
available.description: False until the engine has returned for this job.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the timings come from: always the engine's own `RunMetrics`.

stages.description: The engine's internal stages and how long each took, in order. The engine reports these only for a completed analysis; a refusal or error has none.

stopped_at.title: Stopped At
stopped_at.description: The stage a refusal or error came from, as the engine names it.

n_units_observed.description: How many areas (project and candidates) the engine observed.

n_donors_admitted.title: N Donors Admitted
n_donors_admitted.description: How many comparison areas passed screening.

n_estimator_fits.title: N Estimator Fits
n_estimator_fits.description: How many times the estimator was fitted, placebos included.

EngineMetricsView.title: EngineMetricsView
EngineMetricsView.description: The engine's own timings, taken from ``RunMetrics``. Present only after it returns.

name.title: Name
name.description: The engine's name for the stage.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: How long it took, in milliseconds.

EngineStageTiming.title: EngineStageTiming
EngineStageTiming.description: One of the engine's internal stages and how long it took.

ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode
ErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable failure reasons.

The API maps these to HTTP status codes and the UI maps them to copy, so
neither has to parse an error message. Adding a member is a minor contract
change; changing what one means is a major one.

label.title: Label
label.description: Short human-readable description of the quantity.

value.title: Value
value.description: The measured value, in `unit`. An index (e.g. NDVI) is never a carbon quantity.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: Unit from the declared vocabulary, or '' if none.

confidence.description: The uncertainty interval of the value, when it has one.

provenance.description: How the value was produced: method, inputs, parameters and fingerprint.

state.description: Explicit epistemological status: OBSERVED, DERIVED, MODEL_ESTIMATED, INFERRED, UNAVAILABLE, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

Evidence.title: Evidence
Evidence.description: One auditable value with its unit, uncertainty and origin.

case_id.title: Case Id
case_id.description: The case the evidence is about.

items.title: Items
items.description: Every evidence item, each with its unit, uncertainty and provenance.

verdict.description: The screening verdict, when the engine reached one.

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: Analyst-facing warnings, e.g. that the data is simulated.

EvidenceBundle.title: EvidenceBundle
EvidenceBundle.description:
An immutable, verified collection of evidence for one case.

The bundle is the hand-off point from the deterministic pipeline to the
reporting layer. It is serialisable, diffable and fully reproducible from
its provenance records.

access_level.title: Access Level
access_level.description: The caller's level on this project.

states.title: States
states.description: Record counts by evidence state, across indicators.

climate_status.title: Climate Status
climate_status.description: Whether a climate record is available.

climate_reason.title: Climate Reason
climate_reason.description: Why the climate record is unavailable.

boundary_sha256.title: Boundary Sha256
boundary_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the stored boundary. Absent below the `contribute` level.

items.title: Items
items.description: Every stored annual record. Absent below the `contribute` level.

EvidenceInventoryView.title: EvidenceInventoryView
EvidenceInventoryView.description:
What evidence exists for the project. Everyone sees counts, kinds, states and sources;
checksums, scene ids and the item list need ``EVIDENCE_FULL``.

confidence.description: Its uncertainty interval, when it has one.

EvidenceSnapshot.title: EvidenceSnapshot
EvidenceSnapshot.description: An evidence item as one side of the diff saw it.

EvidenceState.title: EvidenceState
EvidenceState.description: Explicit epistemological status of an evidence item.

ExtractedClaim.title: ExtractedClaim
ExtractedClaim.description: One figure read from the text.

FieldChange.title: FieldChange
FieldChange.description: One field of one evidence item that differs.

org_slug.title: Org Slug
org_slug.description: Slug of the organization to share with.

GrantRequest.description: Share a project with another organization.

org_slug.description: Slug of the organization granted access.

GrantView.title: GrantView
GrantView.description: An active grant of a project to another organization.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: The dotted name of every offending field, e.g. `body.area_ha`.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Identifier of this request, also in the `X-Request-ID` header.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `ok` when the API answers; a failing service answers an error instead.

version.title: Version
version.description: The GroundTruth package version serving this API.

engine_version.title: Engine Version
engine_version.description: Version of the analysis engine every new run uses.

contract_version.title: Contract Version
contract_version.description: Version of the engine contract; results record the one they used.

engine_capabilities.title: Engine Capabilities
engine_capabilities.description: What the engine can actually do, reported by the engine itself.

earth_observation_implemented.title: Earth Observation Implemented
earth_observation_implemented.description: False until the Earth Engine reducer chain lands.

genai_narration_implemented.title: Genai Narration Implemented
genai_narration_implemented.description: False until a narration provider is implemented.

cases_available.title: Cases Available
cases_available.description: How many case definitions this deployment has loaded.

data_origin.title: Data Origin
data_origin.description: Whether the records are real observations or simulated.

IndicatorInventory.title: IndicatorInventory
IndicatorInventory.description: What is stored for one indicator.

InventoryItem.title: InventoryItem
InventoryItem.description: One stored annual record; scene-level detail for EVIDENCE_FULL levels only.

baseline.description: The item in the baseline, if present.

candidate.description: The item in the candidate, if present.

delta.description: ``candidate - baseline`` when both values are numbers.

relative_delta.title: Relative Delta
relative_delta.description: ``delta / |baseline|``; ``None`` when the baseline is zero or not a number.

ItemDiff.title: ItemDiff
ItemDiff.description: One evidence id across the two bundles.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: Identifier of the run that answers the request: new, cached or in flight.

from_cache.title: From Cache
from_cache.description: An existing result answers this request; nothing was queued or will run.

deduplicated.title: Deduplicated
deduplicated.description: An identical job is already queued or running; this is that job.

status_url.title: Status Url
status_url.description: URL to poll for the job's progress.

JobSubmission.title: JobSubmission
JobSubmission.description: What submitting did: queued a new job, or pointed at an existing run.

result_state.title: Result State
result_state.description:
What the run produced: queued, running, measured, refused, failed or cancelled. `refused` is
a scientific outcome; `failed` is a fault.

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.description: True once nothing more will happen; stop polling.

engine_status.title: Engine Status
engine_status.description: What the engine returned, once it ran: completed, refused or error.

is_simulated.title: Is Simulated
is_simulated.description: True for simulated data. Show the simulated-data notice.

attempt.title: Attempt
attempt.description: How many times a worker has taken the job.

max_attempts.title: Max Attempts
max_attempts.description: How many times the job may be tried before it fails for good.

cancel_requested.title: Cancel Requested
cancel_requested.description: True once a cancel was requested. A running job honours it when its worker reaches a checkpoint or the engine returns.

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: The live stage in progress, if one is recorded.

stages.description: Each live stage of the job and its state.

failure_reason.description: Why the job failed, when it failed before the engine produced an error.

status_url.description: URL to poll for this view.

result_url.title: Result Url
result_url.description: Where the stored result is, once there is one.

note.description: How to read the progress fields.
note.default: There is no percentage because none can be known: the analysis engine runs as one step and reports its internal timings only when it finishes. `stages` are observed as they happen; `engine_metrics` fills in afterwards.

JobView.title: JobView
JobView.description:
A job's status and progress, small enough to poll every second.

A **refusal** is a completed job: ``status`` is ``succeeded``, ``result_state`` is
``refused``, ``terminal`` is true and ``error.is_refusal`` is true. It is never
``failed``. ``is_simulated`` and ``data_mode`` are always present, and a simulated job
carries a ``notice``.

user.description: Your account, or null when not signed in.

organizations.title: Organizations
organizations.description: Organizations you belong to, with your role in each.

active_organization.description: The organization you are acting for; null until you choose one (automatic when you belong to exactly one).

MeResponse.title: MeResponse
MeResponse.description: Who you are signed in as, and the organizations you can act for.

role.title: Role
role.description: Their role: owner, admin, member or viewer.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: What went wrong, as a sentence.

code.description:
Machine-readable code, `http_<status>` for this shape (e.g. `http_404`). Act on this, not on
the prose.

is_refusal.description: Always false for this shape: it is never a scientific refusal.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description:
Identifier of this request, also in the `X-Request-ID` header. Quote it when reporting a
problem.

MessageErrorBody.title: MessageErrorBody
MessageErrorBody.description:
An error whose ``detail`` is a plain message, e.g. an unknown case (404).

error envelope, so a client can read the same fields from every error.

code.title: Code
code.description:
different_case, different_data_mode, different_engine_version, different_contract_major,
contract_unreadable or no_bundle.

side.title: Side
side.description: Which run the reason concerns: `baseline`, `candidate` or `both`.

NotComparable.title: NotComparable
NotComparable.description: One reason two runs cannot be compared.

value.title: Value
value.description: Null when nothing was observed that year.

evidence_state.title: Evidence State
evidence_state.description: How the value was obtained: `DERIVED`, `MODEL_ESTIMATED` or `UNAVAILABLE`.

sensor.title: Sensor
sensor.description: Satellite sensor the scenes came from.

clear_pixel_fraction.title: Clear Pixel Fraction
clear_pixel_fraction.description: Share of scene pixels that were clear.

n_scenes.title: N Scenes
n_scenes.description: How many scenes contributed to the year.

aoi_coverage_pct.title: Aoi Coverage Pct

scene_ids.title: Scene Ids

scenes_sha256.title: Scenes Sha256

access_level.description: The caller's level on this project.

ObservationsView.description: The project's annual observations of one indicator.

role.description: Your role in this organization: owner, admin, member or viewer.

PdfExtractResponse.description: The text read from a PDF.

evidence_confidence.description: Null only when the row is degraded.

owner_slug.description: Slug of the organization that owns the project.

ProjectView.description: A project as seen by the active organization (``access_level`` is that org's level).

failure_reason.title: Failure Reason
failure_reason.description: Why a run failed before the engine produced an error.

RunItem.title: RunItem
RunItem.description:
One stored run, as a list or a comparison shows it.

``status`` is the job; ``result_state`` is what happened to the analysis, in the
UI's existing vocabulary. A **refused** run is a successful job (``status`` is
``succeeded``) whose ``result_state`` is ``refused``: a legitimate outcome to
display, never an error. ``is_simulated`` and ``data_mode`` are always present.

items.title: Items
items.description: Runs on this page, newest first.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. Null on the last page.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: The page size that was applied.

contains_simulated.title: Contains Simulated
contains_simulated.description: True if any run on this page is simulated.

RunListPage.title: RunListPage
RunListPage.description: A page of runs, newest first.

stage_durations_ms.title: Stage Durations Ms

n_units_observed.description: Areas observed: the project and its candidate comparisons.

n_estimator_fits.title: N Estimator Fits
n_estimator_fits.description: Times the estimator was fitted, placebos included.

RunMetrics.title: RunMetrics
RunMetrics.description: Timings and counters, for monitoring and capacity planning.

state.title: State
state.description: done | active | pending | skipped (never reached) | failed | unknown (no stage was recorded for this job).

finished_at.title: Finished At

elapsed_ms.title: Elapsed Ms
elapsed_ms.description: Time spent in the active stage so far. A clock reading, not a fraction of anything.

TimelineEvent.description: One lifecycle event of a job.

last_login_at.title: Last Login At

The screening verdicts side by side. Neutral by construction: it states the
two labels and whether they differ, and ranks neither.
